narrative:
The model estimates a 63% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

The strongest influence was that you have received other job opportunities while at your organization. Having external offers is a major signal the model associates with a higher likelihood of leaving, and in your case it strongly pushed the prediction toward departure.

Next, your 6-10 years of experience in your current role worked in your favor. Most employees predicted to stay have only 1-5 years in their organization, so your longer tenure here pulled the prediction back toward staying. However, this positive effect was not enough to overcome the other factors.

Your overall career experience of 6-10 years also contributed to increasing the likelihood of leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only 1-5 years of total experience, your broader background appears to make external moves more feasible in the model’s view.

Taken together, the combination of external opportunities and your solid experience level outweighed the stabilizing effect of your time at the organization. The company may want to discuss retention strategies with you, such as addressing job satisfaction or exploring internal growth paths that could reduce the appeal of outside offers. Understanding these drivers can help both you and the organization make more informed decisions moving forward.
